$comment: ⛔⛔ THE PUBLIC VERSION LADDER. ONE LADDER, AND THIS IS IT.
▶ The private roadmap says it in its own words: 'This is the same ladder published
on the docs site. If one moves, both move.' This file is what makes that
enforceable rather than remembered — docs/index.html is GENERATED from it (by the
site kit, docs/kit/build.mjs), and scripts/check-docs-site.mjs compares it against CHANGELOG.md's 'The ladder'
table on every machine, and against the private roadmap's table as well on a
machine that has one.
⚠ A rung added here and nowhere else fails the gate. A rung added to CHANGELOG
and not here fails it too — it is checked in both directions, because a public
page that is missing a rung and a changelog that has invented one are the same
kind of lie told from opposite ends.
⛔ 'state' is what the site prints beside each rung and there are exactly three:
done    — built and on this branch
planned — specified, not built
goal    — the destination
⚠ It is NOT a claim that a tag exists. Only v0.0.1 and v0.4.0 are tagged, and v1.0.0RC,
which is shelved (the merge, 2026-10-27: kept, never published). The site never says
'released', because charter rule 5 means nothing is.
⛔ 2026-10-28: the merged ladder. v1.0.0b and v1.0.0RC gave way to v0.7.0 … v0.16.0,
then v1.0.0-beta and v1.0.0-rc (each repeats: -beta.1, -beta.2 …), the fleet's spelling.

rungs.summary: Foundation, the CI spine, the licence and the EULA — and an empty window that already installs on three operating systems.
The shell and the audio engine. It looks like Oscillate and it makes a sound.
The project and the arrangement view. It is a DAW.
The editors — piano roll, drum grid, automation, comping, the Cut, Kata, Session Rewind.
Plugin hosting and the stock devices — VST3 and CLAP out of process, and sixty-nine of its own.
The writing tools — the File Explorer, Stem-to-Generators and the export path.
The web go/no-go, the drop onto the timeline, per-device faces and exclusive audio.
The room, core — serverless connection, presence, sync and chat.
The room, live — voice, video, screen share, Takeover, Kumite and the Split Sheet.
Identity — the Lyric Lane, Session Timelapse, session cards and the credits page.

The family look, the same in every Freally app — Blender-rendered knobs, faders and buttons, light and dark on Freally green, interface sounds and a dark title bar — and one instrument library shared with Freally MIDI Master.
One engine — the shared audio and instrument crates pinned at one tag, the next rungs' foundations brought in, and the Freally family's cursor and toggles.
Freally MIDI Master, Flipcopy and Takelight in the box — stock plugins in the browser with a tutorial, MIDI Master's songs dragged onto the arrangement, and exports that carry hosted plugins.
The stage — 3D hands that play any MIDI track, new voices, an amp and a drum machine, and the instrument browser.
Sheets — engraved notation, guitar TAB, the sheet reader, lyrics under the staff, and the PDF.
Lessons — fifteen courses, Show me, and live listening through your own input, graded.
The studio's own — pitch moves, time stretch, live analysis, a doubler and a ducker, a master for each destination, and the final checks.
MixSir — the mix on your phone, paired from a QR code.
New devices, wave one — the low end and the groove.
New devices, wave two — instruments for the sound designer.
New devices, wave three — a record button that reaches back in time, and find-similar across your sounds.
The beta — a new feature freeze, the whole app in one look and 18 languages, and this site rewritten. It repeats until the testing is done. No downloads on this page.
The release candidate — hardening, the full review sweep, and every feature tested in the release app, in Windows' engine and in macOS's and Linux's. It repeats until one survives clean.
Stable and free, with Freally MIDI Master, Flipcopy and Takelight inside. Downloads open later.
